reasoning_traces.think:
Temporal action spotting formalizes action identification in untrimmed videos as a structured regression task: given a video sequence, predict a set of action events with associated timestamps. The mathematical formulation A_n = {a_kn = (c ∈ C, t ∈ [0, L])}_k^A_n encodes discrete actions as tuples of class and time. The method pipeline M = H ∘ N ∘ B defines a compositional architecture where B extracts spatiotemporal features, N refines them, and H produces predictions. Evaluation metrics such as mAP@δ and a-mAP provide scalar measures of model performance by aggregating per-class APs over varying recall thresholds. These primitives enable GSI to generate probabilistic labels and GSE to reason about action dynamics. Failure modes include misalignment between visual cues and timestamps, ambiguity in action classes, and poor generalization due to domain shift. Dualities arise in the trade-off between localization accuracy and classification confidence, while anti-collinearity ensures that distinct action types do not coalesce into indistinguishable representations.
